A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Locphylax work and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Existing material can be matched through page reflow and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: Section 4 and the appendices report original defense evaluations, attention-head ablations, case studies, and representation analyses.

after.justification: The original empirical results are retained, and Appendix C adds a test-time defense comparison and syntactic-trigger results in Table 7.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same known-trigger injection, clustering objective, loss balancing, and recovery fine-tuning procedure (Section 3, Equations 5–8). Calling the existing injected response a neutral target in v2 clarifies its description without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix C adds an implicit syntactic-trigger scenario on AdvBench. AdvBench already appears in v1's explicit-phrase attack with delayed harmful output (Section 4.4), so this extends trigger conditions within an existing dataset; the other benchmark coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Table 7 adds Mo et al. (2025)'s Test-time Backdoor Mitigation as an evaluated comparator on SST2 and the syntactic-trigger scenario. Existing comparisons with SFT, Fine-Mixing, NAD/Distillation, and PDB remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The added syntactic experiment uses Llama3-8B-Instruct, poisons 5% of AdvBench, and transforms queries using a specified syntactic template. This introduces a protocol for the new experiment; previously reported training settings, metrics, and evaluation procedures are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds a targeted robustness test asking whether Locphylax handles implicit syntactic triggers. The existing delayed-output attack, attention-head ablations, case studies, and t-SNE analyses are retained, including material moved from Appendices C/D to D/E.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Table 7 follows the existing point-estimate reporting practice; the retained averages and ranges across attention heads are unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 7 adds comparator scores and syntactic-trigger results: Locphylax reports 23.07% ASR and 99.61% CACC, versus 41.15% and 99.03% for the test-time defense. Its Locphylax SST2 entries repeat Table 1's values. Earlier numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The threat-model formulations, injection and recovery objectives, clustering loss, and uniform-attention ablation formula remain unchanged (Equations 1–9). No theorem, proof, or mathematical derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same aggregation discovery, trigger-agnostic defense contribution, and generalization claims, including average ASR of 4.41% and clean-performance preservation within 0.5%. The added experiment supports the existing claims without revising their stated scope.

C2.justification: Appendix C newly interprets the results as robustness to implicit syntactic triggers and superiority over the test-time defense. Its claim of superiority across all metrics overstates Table 7: Phrase CACC is 95.40% versus the comparator's 95.80%. Section 8 also adds a method-specific dual-use discussion; existing mechanism explanations and multimodal limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link in the abstract and a syntactic-poisoning recipe with a template and example query transformation in Appendix C. Existing training configurations are retained. The PDFs establish the added access information, but do not establish the repository's contents or functionality.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hidden Killer (Qi et al., 2021) and the test-time defense (Mo et al., 2025) to support the new evaluation, and replaces several introductory background citations. The central positioning around backdoor aggregation and trigger-agnostic mitigation remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 updates affiliations and correspondence information, makes localized wording edits, and adds acknowledgements, an ethical statement, and Appendix C. The case-study and t-SNE appendices become D and E. Most existing scientific prose and narrative organization are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 7, adjusts Figure 1's typography and legend presentation, removes its bottom annotation, and rearranges the case-study boxes. Other figures and existing table structures are retained, with page reflow and relocation.

improvement.justification: Appendix C tests the trigger-agnostic claim beyond explicit trigger strings and adds a relevant test-time comparator, addressing limited gaps in v1's evaluation. The code pointer also improves access documentation. These are modest gains: the method and original evidence remain unchanged, comparator implementation details are sparse, and the new claim of superiority on every metric contradicts Table 7's Phrase CACC values.
